title: Outvoted at home: roll calls the district supervisor lost
question: On which votes about their own district was the district supervisor on the losing side?
finding: The district’s own supervisor was on the losing side of 11 roll calls on matters naming that district, out of 32 divided ones and 575 in all (appeal of a conditional-use decision 6; appeal of an environmental-review decision 5). Most often: Katy Tang (4); Matt Haney (3); Hillary Ronen (2); Danny Sauter (1).
how: From the roll calls in the previous table: a vote is “lost” when the district supervisor voted no and the motion passed, or voted aye and it failed. One vote printed on several sibling files of an appeal is listed once, under the appeal’s hearing file. Votes to postpone are included and are labelled.
limits: Losing a vote is ordinary legislative business and says nothing about the merits. Several of these are procedural votes taken minutes before the deciding vote, and the record shows motions on conditional-use appeals failing with more ayes than noes, so some need more than a bare majority. The table has no street addresses; the linked file gives the full record. A difference between areas, or between groups of cases, is not proof of bias. Areas differ in what is proposed, in zoning, lot sizes, building ages and land prices, and in who chooses to apply, object or appeal at all.
